```{r setup, include = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
## load packages
packs.html <- c("knitr", "pander", "reporttools", "dplyr", "readxl")
for (i in 1:length(packs.html)){library(packs.html[i], character.only = TRUE)}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

## talks
path <- getwd()
talks <- as.data.frame(read_excel(paste(path, "/data/seminars.xlsx", sep = ""), col_types = NULL))

# prepare date strings
d <- substr(talks$date, 1, 2)
m <- substr(talks$date, 4, 5)
y <- substr(talks$date, 7, 11)

rdate <- paste(y, m, d, sep = "")
talks$rdate <- rdate

# select talks with past date
talks <- (talks %>% filter(rdate > gsub("-", "", as.character(Sys.Date()))) %>% filter(!is.na(date)))

talks <- (talks %>% group_by(rdate, talknr)  %>% 
        arrange(
            rdate, 
            talknr
        ))
talks <- as.data.frame(talks)
rdate <- unique(talks$rdate)
dates <- unique(select(talks, date))[, 1]
```

## ASA Biopharmaceutical Section Webinar: Embedding Estimands in ICH M11: From Framework to Practice

**Link & Details:** [Register Here](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/asabiop/asa-biop-distance-learning-webinar-series-oct-30)  
**Date:** Friday, October 30, 2026  
**Time:** 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM EDT  
**Location:** Online (Free to attend)  
**Organizer:** North America Estimands Implementation Working Group (NA EIWG), ASA Biopharmaceutical Section  

---

### Abstract

ICH M11, the Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP) guideline, establishes a globally harmonised approach to the structure, content, and electronic exchange of clinical trial protocols. Its three interconnected components—the Guideline, Protocol Template, and Technical Specification—are intended to improve protocol quality, clarity, consistency, and efficiency across sponsors, investigators, ethics committees, and regulators.

The ICH E9(R1) Addendum introduced the estimand framework to improve alignment among clinical trial objectives, design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation. As organizations continue to implement estimands in practice, adoption of the M11 protocol template presents an important opportunity to embed estimand thinking directly into protocol development and support more consistent multidisciplinary decision-making.

This webinar, organized by the ASA Biopharmaceutical Section's North America Estimands Implementation Working Group (NA EIWG), will explore practical approaches to implementing the estimand framework within the M11 protocol template. Several speakers and panelists were directly involved in the development of ICH M11, bringing firsthand perspectives on its intent and practical application. 
Webinar participants will discuss:
* M11’s inclusion of clearly defined clinical questions and estimand tables.
* How its objective-based protocol structure—rather than the traditional endpoint-based approach—can strengthen alignment of trial objectives and their corresponding estimands with trial design, analysis, and reporting.
* Implementation challenges, opportunities, and emerging practices across industry and health authorities.

> The NA EIWG brings together stakeholders from industry, health authorities, and academia to share experiences, identify implementation challenges, and advance practical solutions for estimand implementation.
